lessons.title: NYSE and Nasdaq: How the World's Largest Stock Market Is Built

children.text: On 12 June 2026, SpaceX became a public company in the largest IPO in history, raising $75 billion and more than doubling the record Saudi Aramco set in 2019. It listed on Nasdaq. Six months earlier, Walmart, a NYSE company for over five decades, had packed up and moved its listing to Nasdaq too. Two exchanges a few kilometres apart in New York are locked in a fierce fight for the world's most valuable companies. Think of it as NSE vs BSE, but where the prize is Nvidia, Apple and the next trillion-dollar IPO. To read the US market, you first need to know how its two giants actually work, and why they are only part of the story.

body.text: The US stock market is not one exchange. It is two listing giants, dozens of competing trading venues and a large off-exchange network, all tied together by rules that force every trade towards the best available price in the country.

children.text: Two Giants, One City

body.title: SpaceX in rupees
body.prompt: SpaceX sold about 555.6 million shares at $135 each, raising about $75 billion. At USD/INR 95, how much is $75 billion in ₹ lakh crore? Round to two decimal places.
body.explanation: First check the size: 555.6 million × $135 = $75.0 billion. Then convert: $75 billion × 95 = ₹7,125 billion = ₹7.125 trillion. Since ₹1 lakh crore = ₹1 trillion, that is about ₹7.13 lakh crore, or ₹7,12,500 crore. That is roughly 25 times Hyundai Motor India's ₹27,870 crore IPO.

children.text: How a Trade Happens on Each

markDefs.definition: A trading firm assigned by NYSE to each listed stock. It is obliged to maintain a fair and orderly market, helps run the opening and closing auctions, and steps in with its own capital when buyers and sellers are out of balance.
A firm that continuously quotes prices at which it will buy and sell a stock, earning the gap between the two. On Nasdaq, many market makers compete to quote the same stock.

children.text: Most trading on both exchanges today is electronic, and a Zerodha user would recognise the basic order book. The difference is in who keeps the market orderly. On NYSE, each stock has one
Designated Market Maker
with formal obligations, supported by a human trading floor that is most active at the open, the close and during big news. On Nasdaq, there is no single firm in charge. Instead, several
market makers

compete to quote the best prices. Both exchanges run opening and closing auctions, where buy and sell orders are matched at a single price. NSE has recently moved closer to this model. It has long run a pre-open call auction, and since 3 August 2026 it also runs a Closing Auction Session for stocks that trade in F&O. Other NSE stocks still close at a weighted average price of the last 30 minutes of trading.

body.text: The closing auction matters enormously in the US. Index funds and ETFs want to trade at the official closing price because that is the price their index uses. So a large chunk of each day's volume is saved for the final auction, and on index rebalancing days the closing minutes can be the busiest of the entire session.

body.title: How does NSE set its close?
body.question: An investor used to US markets asks how NSE decides the official closing price of Reliance Industries, a stock with F&O contracts, after 3 August 2026. What is the correct answer?
options: The price of the very last trade before 3:30 pm
A closing auction run by a Designated Market Maker
A Closing Auction Session from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm, where orders are matched at the single price that executes the most volume
The average of the day's high and low prices
body.explanation: Since 3 August 2026, F&O stocks on NSE trade continuously until 3:15 pm and then enter a Closing Auction Session until 3:35 pm. Orders are collected and matched at the equilibrium price where the maximum volume can trade. Stocks without F&O contracts still close at the weighted average price of the last 30 minutes. NSE's auction has no Designated Market Maker; those exist only on NYSE.

children.text: Beyond the Big Two: A Fragmented Market

markDefs.definition: A private trading venue where orders are not displayed publicly before they execute. Large institutions use them to buy or sell big blocks of shares without tipping off the market.
A trading firm, such as Citadel Securities or Virtu, that executes retail brokers' orders internally instead of sending them to an exchange, often paying the broker for that order flow.
National Best Bid and Offer. The highest buy price and lowest sell price for a stock across all US exchanges at any moment. US rules require trades to happen at this price or better.

children.text: Here is the part that surprises most Indian investors. An Apple share listed on Nasdaq can trade on NYSE's electronic venues, on Cboe's exchanges, on the Texas Stock Exchange, or away from any exchange entirely. The US has 29 registered national securities exchanges, counting options exchanges, after the SEC approved the Texas Stock Exchange in September 2025. It began live trading in July 2026. On top of that, around half of all US share volume is executed off-exchange, in
dark pools
or by
wholesalers
. What holds this maze together is the
NBBO
, a single national best price that every venue must respect.

body.title: Where your order goes: US vs India

columns.label: United States
points: A stock can trade on dozens of exchanges and off-exchange venues
Retail orders from apps like Robinhood are often sent to wholesalers, not exchanges
Brokers can receive payment for order flow from wholesalers
Around half of share volume trades off-exchange
The NBBO links all venues into one national best price

columns.label: India
points: Listed shares trade on recognised stock exchanges, mainly NSE and BSE
Your Zerodha or Groww order goes straight to the exchange order book
No wholesalers buying retail order flow
No dark pools; even large block deals go through a special exchange window
NSE handles the overwhelming majority of cash market turnover

body.title: Share of India's cash equity market turnover, FY26 (%)

body.text: Do not assume US prices are set only on NYSE or Nasdaq screens. With around half of volume off-exchange, the price you see on a chart is stitched together from many venues. Payment for order flow also means a US app can be commission-free while earning from how it routes your orders. In India, your broker earns through brokerage and fees, and your order sits on a public exchange order book.

body.title: The national price
body.textWithBlank: The highest bid and lowest offer for a stock across all US exchanges is called the National Best Bid and ___, or NBBO.
body.explanation: NBBO stands for National Best Bid and Offer. US rules under Regulation NMS require that trades are not executed at prices worse than the best displayed prices across exchanges, which keeps a fragmented market behaving like one market.

children.text: The Battle for Listings

In India, a large company almost always lists on both NSE and BSE. In the US, a company picks one primary listing exchange, and that choice is a matter of brand, fees and identity. NYSE sells tradition, its trading floor and the famous opening bell. Nasdaq sells a technology and innovation image. Nasdaq organises its listings into three tiers: the Global Select Market for the largest companies, the Global Market, and the Capital Market for smaller companies. NYSE has its main board and NYSE American for smaller firms. Companies can and do switch. Walmart's move in December 2025 told investors it wanted to be seen as a technology-driven retailer, not just a store chain.
Indian Companies on Wall Street

markDefs.definition: American Depositary Receipt. A certificate traded on a US exchange in dollars that represents a fixed number of shares of a foreign company held by a custodian bank in the home country.

children.text: Some of India's best-known companies also trade in New York through
ADRs

. Infosys became the first Indian company to list on Nasdaq in 1999 and later moved its ADRs to NYSE. Each ADR represents a fixed number of the company's Indian shares, so its dollar price should roughly track the NSE price converted at the exchange rate. Because ADRs trade while India sleeps, they are often the first market reaction to results announced after NSE closes.

body.latex: \text{ADR parity (\$)} = \frac{\text{NSE price (₹)} \times \text{Shares per ADR}}{\text{USD/INR}} \qquad \text{Premium} = \left(\frac{\text{ADR price}}{\text{ADR parity}} - 1\right) \times 100
body.caption: How to check whether an ADR trades above or below its Indian share price

body.title: Find the ADR premium
body.prompt: Illustrative prices: Infosys closes at ₹1,500 on NSE. One Infosys ADR represents one Indian share. USD/INR is 95. The Infosys ADR trades at $16.50 on NYSE. What is the ADR premium over its Indian share price, in percent? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: ADR parity = ₹1,500 × 1 ÷ 95 = $15.79. Premium = ($16.50 ÷ $15.79 − 1) × 100 = (1.0450 − 1) × 100 = 4.5%. The ADR is priced 4.5% above what the same share costs on NSE. Premiums like this can persist because moving shares between the Indian and US markets involves regulatory limits, costs and time.

body.title: Results after the bell
body.scenario: Infosys announces its quarterly results at 4:15 pm IST, after NSE has closed. Revenue growth guidance is cut. At 7:00 pm IST, when NYSE opens, the Infosys ADR (INFY) falls 6%. Overnight, the Nasdaq ends flat and the rupee is unchanged. You hold Infosys shares in your Zerodha account.
body.prompt: What does the ADR move tell you about how Infosys might open on NSE the next morning, and what else should you check before 9:15 am?
body.modelAnswer:
1. The ADR is the first place global investors could react to the results, so a 6% fall is a strong signal that Infosys is likely to open lower on NSE.
2. With the rupee unchanged, the currency is not distorting the move, so most of the 6% reflects the results themselves.
3. The Nasdaq was flat, so this is company news, not a broad market mood swing.
4. The Indian open will not necessarily match the ADR exactly. The ADR may already carry a premium, and Indian institutions and retail investors will form their own views in the pre-open auction.
5. Before 9:15 am, check: where INFY closed at 1:30 am IST, whether its premium to parity changed, GIFT Nifty, how peers like Wipro's ADR moved, and analyst commentary on the guidance cut. Then decide based on your view of the business, not just the overnight price.

body.title: Map a US stock in five minutes
steps: Pick a US company you know, such as Nvidia or JPMorgan, and find its primary listing exchange on nasdaq.com or nyse.com.
Note which Nasdaq tier or NYSE board it trades on.
Pick one Indian ADR from the table and note its ticker, exchange and shares per ADR.
Take its latest NSE closing price from Kite or screener.in and today's USD/INR rate, and calculate ADR parity.
Compare parity with the ADR's last price and note whether it trades at a premium or a discount.

cards.definition: The single firm assigned to each NYSE stock, responsible for a fair and orderly market and for helping run the opening and closing auctions.
A firm that continuously quotes buy and sell prices for a stock. On Nasdaq, many market makers compete for each stock.
A single-price match of buy and sell orders at the end of the US trading day. It sets the official close used by index funds.
A private venue where orders are not displayed before execution, used mainly for large institutional trades.
A firm such as Citadel Securities or Virtu that executes retail orders off-exchange, often paying brokers for the order flow.
National Best Bid and Offer. The best buy and sell prices across all US exchanges, which trades must respect.
American Depositary Receipt. A dollar-traded US certificate representing a fixed number of a foreign company's shares, such as HDB for HDFC Bank.

points: NYSE (about $31 trillion) and Nasdaq (about $35 trillion) are the world's two largest exchanges and compete hard for listings, as SpaceX's $75 billion Nasdaq IPO and Walmart's move to Nasdaq show.
NYSE uses a hybrid model with one Designated Market Maker per stock and a trading floor. Nasdaq is fully electronic with competing market makers.

Both US exchanges set official closing prices through auctions. NSE introduced a Closing Auction Session for F&O stocks on 3 August 2026, while other NSE stocks still close at a last-30-minute weighted average.
The US market is fragmented: 29 registered exchanges including options venues, and around half of share volume trades off-exchange in dark pools or with wholesalers.
The NBBO ties every US venue to a single national best price.
India is centralised: orders go to exchange order books, there is no payment for order flow, and NSE handled 92.9% of cash turnover in FY26.
Infosys, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Wipro and Dr. Reddy's trade in New York as ADRs, which often give the first reaction to news released after NSE closes.
